messages:
maria: quick question — for the next two sprints do we want to split work by customer hotpaths (P0 bug fixes) vs product delight (tiny UX + perf)? leaning to 60/40 bug-first for customer-facing flows.
aj: +1 for bug-first on core flows. if we do 60/40 we need a clear definition of what counts as a bug vs an enhancement to avoid scope creep.
sanjay: can we use the severity + user-visible regression rule we used in Q1? severity >= S2 or any customer-reported production regression -> bug lane.
ellie: agree but also flag small UX regressions that reduce retention as bugs (e.g., streaming UI stalls). otherwise we end up paying later.
maria: good call. proposal: define buckets: Bug (prod regression/customer-reported S1/S2), Stability (non-user-impacting infra/latency), Enhancement (new behaviors/visual polish). allocate sprint slices 60% Bug+Stability, 40% Enhancement.
kevin: ops question — how many can we realistically land per sprint if we keep canaries and rollbacks? current velocity shows ~8 medium+ fixes per sprint. with 60% commit that’s ~5-6 fixes.
aj: right. also need to carve out 1 dev-day per engineer for on-call followups; that reduces available capacity. we should adjust point budgets.
maria: action item: aj + kevin to recalc sprint budget with 1 dev-day buffer and share recommended slice sizes by EOD.
ops-bot: Deploy Canary for hotfixes scheduled at 05:00 UTC (automated message).
sanjay: quick thought — can we use a gated backlog where enhancements require an acceptance test (perf or retention signal) before being allowed into the 40%? prevents speculative tweaks.
ellie: I can draft an acceptance checklist: impact hypothesis, measurable metric, QA steps, rollout plan. will share a template.
aj: we should also reserve a single enhancement ticket as "quick-win" each sprint (<= 4hrs) to keep morale and customer love.
maria: agreed. prioritize enhs by expected retention/usage delta. if impact unknown move to research spike first.
kevin: final ask — for dedicated customers with SLAs, do we treat their escalations as guaranteed bug lane overrides?
maria: yes — customer escalations for SLA customers are auto-prioritized into current sprint if they meet the regression definition. note this may bump some enhancements.
sanjay: ok locking that.
kevin: aj + maria — can you both confirm the list of SLA customers and routing plan so support knows the escalation path?
aj: will pull list and post in #support by lunchtime.
maria: timeline: today -> agree definitions and point budgets; tomorrow -> grooming session to tag top 10 bug candidates and top 6 enhs; next Tue -> start sprint.
ellie: I’ll prep the enhancement acceptance template before the groom.
maria: thanks everyone. short follow-up thread: please add any specific customer asks as replies here or tag me.
